title: Initialize a repository
description: Run `git init` inside your workspace to create a new Git repository.

title: Make your first commit
description: Create any file, `git add` it, and commit it with any message.

title: Check repository status
description: Modify a tracked file and run `git status` to see it listed as changed. (We just check that a commit history exists and working tree has been touched.)

title: Create a new branch named 'dev'
description: Run `git branch dev` or `git checkout -b dev` to create a branch called 'dev'.

title: Switch to the 'dev' branch
description: Run `git checkout dev` (or `git switch dev`) so HEAD points at 'dev'.

title: Merge 'dev' into 'main'
description: Switch back to main and merge dev into it.

title: Stash your changes
description: Modify a tracked file, then run `git stash` to shelve the change.

title: Tag a commit
description: Create an annotated or lightweight tag named `v1.0` on your current commit: `git tag v1.0`.

title: Delete the 'dev' branch
description: Now that dev is merged, clean it up: `git branch -d dev`.

title: Rebase a branch
description: Create a branch called `feature`, add at least one commit on it, then run `git rebase main` while on `feature` so its commit(s) sit cleanly on top of main's history.

title: Cherry-pick a commit
description: Switch to `main`, find a commit hash from `feature` (`git log feature --oneline`), and run `git cherry-pick <hash>` to bring just that commit onto main.

title: Clone from the practice remote
description: Clone your personal bare repo from the git-server: `git clone git://git-server/<your-id>/practice.git`.

title: Push to the remote
description: Commit a change on `main` and push it: `git push origin main`.

title: Pull from the remote
description: Make a change directly in the bare repo from another clone (or just run `git fetch origin && git merge origin/main`), then confirm your local main is in sync by running `git pull origin main`.

title: Resolve a merge conflict
description: Create two branches that each edit the same line of the same file differently, merge one into the other, resolve the conflict markers by hand, `git add` the fixed file, and complete the merge with `git commit`.
